risks: Implementation cannot be complete within only the six named surface areas: Task/Review domain validators, live SQLite constraints, and Console rendering are genuine required expansions and need authorization before implementation.

Removing SQLite CHECK constraints requires a foreign-keys-off table rebuild with exact recreation of dependent indexes/triggers; incomplete recreation could weaken ownership or immutability guarantees.

Input MCP schemas cannot safely enumerate only the current allowlist because exported schemas are shared by both adapters, while output schemas must also describe historical selections no longer enabled. Use a generic bounded model-ID schema and enforce membership at runtime.

availableModels currently declares maxItems 8 while runtime/Desktop allow no count bound. The shared validator should enforce 1–8 distinct IDs, or the schema limit must be deliberately changed everywhere.
The CLI currently silently falls back to defaults for malformed or partially supplied lists, which can unexpectedly broaden access; strict startup failure is the safer behavior.
Codex client sets modelProvider to openai for every explicit model, so dynamic IDs remain OpenAI/Codex model identifiers, not arbitrary provider routing.

A persisted Task or Review may reference a valid model removed from the current allowlist. Output schemas and Console rendering must continue accepting/displaying that historical value while new selections are rejected.
verificationTargets: Shared validator accepts current defaults and a new valid ID, rejects empty/whitespace/comma/control-character/overlength IDs, duplicates, and more than eight configured models.
Desktop saves, reloads, renders, and forwards an arbitrary valid model ID while preserving order and deduplication; invalid lists leave prior settings intact.
Direct Core startup accepts a custom valid model and rejects malformed explicit configuration without default fallback.
CurrentWorkflow and both MCP adapters expose the configured custom model in availableModels.
MCP schemas contain no three-model enums, remain closed objects, accept bounded custom IDs, and runtime errors still include authoritative candidates.
Control API accepts configured custom Task and Review selections and rejects syntactically valid but disabled IDs.
Fresh schema and v28→v29 migration both accept custom model values, preserve existing Task/Review rows, report schema version 29, and pass PRAGMA foreign_key_check.
Console renders default models with friendly labels and custom valid models verbatim.
Coordinator and Codex client forward the custom ID unchanged through thread/start and turn/start.
